page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is an x86_64 virtual server belonging to the High Performance family. It is configured with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 12.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB of RAM per core, and 260 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in stress-ng single-core (2427.57) and multi-core (9526.81) tests, alongside average results in passmark CPU encryption (3738.58) and small-block cached memory bandwidth (380.64 GB/sec). However, the server exhibits weak performance in large-block memory bandwidth (24.31 GB/sec read, 20.91 GB/sec write) and Passmark CPU scores (6640.94). Bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations fall into the poor category, reflecting performance limitations under sustained database or compression workloads.

Due to its shared CPU allocation, this server presents a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The 260 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local storage, but the weak memory bandwidth and database benchmark scores suggest it is less suited for high-throughput database operations. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, light text processing, small-scale LLM text generation, and general-purpose development or testing environments where resource sharing is acceptable.
